name: Surf Equipment Rental Damage Claims
description: You rent a surfboard from one of the many rental stands along Biarritz's beaches. When you return it, the operator scrutinizes the board and 'discovers' a ding or crack that they claim you caused. They demand €50-100 for repairs. The damage may have been pre-existing and hidden, or it may be standard wear they use to extract money.
avoidance: Before accepting any rental equipment, photograph it from all angles with your phone's timestamp visible. Ask the operator to note any existing damage on the rental agreement. Use established, well-reviewed rental companies rather than informal beach stands.
location: Surf rental shops along Grande Plage, Cote des Basques equipment hire, beachfront rental stands

name: Bus and Public Transport Pickpocketing
description: Biarritz's Chronoplus buses are generally safe, but pickpockets target crowded routes serving beaches and tourist areas. During the press of boarding or when standing in a packed bus during summer, a skilled thief slips a hand into your bag or pocket. They often work in pairs: one bumps or distracts, the other steals.
avoidance: Keep bags zipped and held in front of you, not hanging off your shoulder. Use a money belt for passport and large amounts of cash. Keep phone in a front pocket, not a loose jacket pocket. Stay alert when boarding and exiting.
location: Bus lines serving Grande Plage and city center, crowded Chronoplus buses, train station platforms

name: Crit'Air Environmental Sticker Fine Trap
description: Tourists renting cars in Germany to visit Alsace often discover their vehicles lack the French Crit'Air environmental sticker required for driving in Strasbourg's Low Emission Zone. Only the registered vehicle owner can request a sticker, making it impossible for tourists with foreign rentals to obtain one legally. Fines reach up to 135 euros.
avoidance: Rent cars within France to ensure Crit'Air compliance. Park outside Strasbourg and use trams (free parking available in Kehl, Germany). Confirm sticker status before driving into any French city center. Use train connections between Colmar and Strasbourg instead of driving.
location: Strasbourg city center Low Emission Zone, German border crossings, routes from Basel/Freiburg

name: Currency Exchange and Dynamic Conversion Ripoff
description: Exchange bureaus in tourist areas advertise 'no commission' but hide costs in unfavorable exchange rates, effectively charging up to 15% in hidden fees. When paying by card, merchants may offer 'Dynamic Currency Conversion' to charge in your home currency - accepting this means paying inflated rates.
avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks for best exchange rates. Always choose to pay in Euros when card terminals offer a choice. Compare rates online before exchanging any cash. Use a travel card with no foreign transaction fees.
location: Colmar train station exchange kiosk, tourist area exchange bureaus, card payment terminals

name: Island Hotel Quality Trap
description: Hotels on the island charge premium prices for substandard accommodation and dining. Guests report surly staff, terrible restaurant food, and exhausting logistics - climbing seven flights of stairs with luggage after a quarter-mile walk from the shuttle. With no competition and a captive audience, hotels have no incentive to improve.
avoidance: Stay in mainland hotels across the causeway instead. Visit as a day trip rather than overnight. If staying on-island, pack light and be prepared for physical exertion. Eat dinner on the mainland before retiring to island accommodation.
location: All hotels on Mont-Saint-Michel island, L'Auberge Saint Pierre

name: Souvenir Shop Overpricing
description: Mont-Saint-Michel's souvenir shops have been overcharging tourists since medieval times - literally. The narrow Grande Rue is packed with shops selling overpriced trinkets and generic souvenirs. One commenter noted that 'shops on MSM have been fleecing tourists since at least the middle ages.'
avoidance: Accept that you'll pay tourist prices if buying anything. Limit purchases to genuinely local items: Breton cookies, calvados, mariniere shirts. Buy souvenirs in Pontorson or other mainland towns instead. The Abbey gift shop has more curated, quality items.
location: Grande Rue souvenir shops, gift shops throughout the island

name: Tram Ticket Enforcement Trap
description: Montpellier enforces strict ticket validation rules. Tourists who purchase valid tickets but don't validate them immediately upon boarding face fines. Officers have been reported to use intimidating tactics. Unlike other French cities, Montpellier's system requires immediate validation.
avoidance: Always validate your ticket immediately upon boarding - before finding a seat. Keep validated tickets until you exit the tram. Consider using contactless payment cards which auto-validate. Purchase tickets via the TAM app.
location: All tram lines, particularly busy tram stops

name: Les Halles Castellane Market Pickpocketing
description: Montpellier's popular markets draw crowds and pickpockets alike. The bustling atmosphere, narrow aisles between stalls, and shoppers focused on produce create ideal conditions for theft. Pickpockets work alone or in teams, using the crowd and natural jostling as cover.
avoidance: Wear bags closed and in front of your body. Don't put phones or wallets in back pockets. Be extra alert when examining goods at stalls. Keep shopping bags closed and close to your body.
location: Les Halles Castellane, Plan Cabanes market, Marche du Lez, street markets

name: Distraction Theft / Bump and Lift
description: Thieves work in teams using distraction techniques. One person creates a diversion - dropping something, asking for directions, bumping into you 'accidentally,' or causing a commotion - while an accomplice steals your valuables. The bump happens so naturally that victims don't realize they've been robbed until the thieves have vanished.
avoidance: Keep moving if someone tries to stop you unnecessarily. If someone bumps you, immediately check your valuables. Don't get drawn into distractions. Wear bags across your body with zippers facing inward.
location: Busy pedestrian streets in the Ecusson, Esplanade de l'Europe, tram boarding areas

name: Nighttime Saint-Roch Area Crime
description: The area between Montpellier's historic Ecusson district and the Saint-Roch train station has a bad reputation at night. After nightlife crowds disperse (especially after 2 AM), opportunistic crime increases in the quieter streets. Tourists walking back to hotels near the station face elevated risk of confrontation or robbery.
avoidance: Take taxis or ride-sharing after late nights out. Stick to well-lit, busy main streets. Don't walk alone late at night. Stay in central, well-connected neighborhoods.
location: Streets between Ecusson and Gare Saint-Roch, around the train station after dark
